exposure: Clinical and pathological data (stage, tumor size, grade, histological type, stromal invasion, lymphovascular space involvement)
outcome: Oncologic insufficiency (necessity for additional oncologic treatment following RT)
cohort: The study participants were 24 patients who underwent radical trachelectomy for early-stage cervical cancer at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, University of Debrecen.
finding: Most cases of oncologically insufficient radical trachelectomies possess significant risk features (such as stage IB1 or greater, tumor size > 2 cm or > 15mm, G3, nonsquamous/adeno histological type, stromal invasion > 9 mm, and lymphovascular space involvement) that can be identified preoperatively.
